text: 1.3.1 Definitions
trace: 1.3 Definitions and Abbreviations --> 1.3.1 Definitions

text:
* For the purposes of the present document, the terms and definitions given in 3GPP TR 21.905 \[1\] and the following
  * apply. A term defined in the present document takes precedence over the definition of the same term, if any, in 3GPP
  * TR 21.905 \[2\]. For the base station classes of Pico, Micro and Macro, the definitions are given in 3GPP TR 38.104 \[3\].
  * Carrier Frequency: Center frequency of the cell.
  * F1 interface: The open interface between O-CU and O-DU7-2 as defined by 3GPP TS 38.473 between CU and DU.
  * Integrated architecture: In the integrated architecture, the O-RU and O-DUx are implemented on one platform. Each
  * O-RU and RF front end is associated with one O-DU7-2. They are then aggregated to O-CU and connected by F1
  * interface.
  * Split architecture: The O-RUx and O-DUx are physically separated from one another in this architecture. A switch may
  * aggregate multiple O-RUxs to one O-DUx. O-DUx switch and O-RUxs are connected by the fronthaul interface as
  * defined in WG4.
  * Transmission Reception Point \(TRxP\): Antenna array with one or more antenna elements available to the network
  * located at a specific geographical location for a specific area.

text: Chapter 2 Hardware Reference Design 1
trace: Chapter 2 Hardware Reference Design 1

text:
* This chapter describes a white box hardware reference design example for indoor Picocell deployment scenario. It
  * includes O-CU, O-DU7-2 and FHM7-2/FHGW7-2→8 for IPC deployment scenario.
trace: Chapter 2 Hardware Reference Design 1

text: 2.1 O-CU Hardware Reference Design
trace: 2.1 O-CU Hardware Reference Design

text:
* The O-CU white box hardware is the platform that perform the O-CU function of upper L2 and L3. The hardware
  * systems specified in this document meet the computing, power and environmental requirements of use cases
  * configurations and feature sets of RAN physical node. These requirements are described in the early hardware
  * requirement specification as well as in the use cases document. The O-CU hardware includes the chassis platform,

text: 2.2.3.2 Hardware Accelerator
trace: 7 2.2.3 O-DU7-2 Hardware Components -->  --> 2.2.3.2 Hardware Accelerator

text:
* Hardware accelerators can be used in O-DU7-2 to offload computationally intensive functions and to optimize the performance under varying traffic and loading conditions. The acceleration functional requirements and implementation are system designer's choice; however, the O-DU7-2 shall meet the minimum system performance requirements under various loading and deployment conditions. In most cases, a Field Programmable Gate Array \(FPGA\) or Application Specific Integrated Circuit \(ASIC\) based PCIe card can be used to optimize the system performance. The FPGA\(s\) are part of a Network Interface Controller \(NIC\) that further provides connectivity services.
  * 2.2.3.2.1 Accelerator Design Solution 1
  * Channel coding for Low-Density Parity Codes \(LDPC\) and fronthaul compression requires a significant amount of bit level processing and is well suited to a fine-grained FPGA architecture and/or low cost/power structured ASIC. Options include:
  * Virtualization: Multi-channel DMA, Virtual machine integration, load balancing functions
  * Look-aside FEC: LDPC \(de\)coding, Polar \(de\)coding, Rate \(De\)Matcher, \(De\) Interleaver, Cyclic Redundancy Check \(CRC\), Hybrid Automatic Repeat request \(HARQ\) retransmission
  * Bump-in-wire Fronthaul: compression / decompression for latency and bandwidth reduction
  * a. Accelerator Requirements

text: 5 Functional offload requirements:
trace: 7 2.2.3 O-DU7-2 Hardware Components -->  --> 2.2.3.2 Hardware Accelerator --> 5 Functional offload requirements:

text: One of the candidate functions for offloading is the LDPC encoder and decoder, which typically consists of computationally intensive and relatively highly power consuming functions. It must be noted that neither software implementation in CPU nor soft FPGA logic implementation would provide a highly power efficient solution while meeting/exceeding 3GPP NR user-plane encoder/decoder throughput and latency requirements, rather a hardened implementation of the FEC functions would be very power efficient. Downlink and uplink throughputs of up to 40Gbps and 18Gbps, respectively, are shown feasible with this architecture. Other candidate L1 functions for acceleration include CRC generation, segmentation, bit-level/sub-block interleaving and scrambling as well as FFT/IFFT processing, for which an FPGA can be used.
trace: 7 2.2.3 O-DU7-2 Hardware Components -->  --> 2.2.3.2 Hardware Accelerator --> 5 Functional offload requirements:

text: 14 For other symbol processing L1 functions which require heavy multiply and accumulation operations, FPGAs 15 1 and 2 have DSP blocks that can efficiently perform these operations. Polar encoding and/or decoding on the 16 control-plane can also be offloaded to FPGA 1 resulting in high throughputs and low latencies.

They support both PCIe Gen3 x16 or PCIe Gen4 x8, which allow the FPGA device to interface with any GPP supporting either PCIe Gen3 x16 or PCIe Gen4 x8 interface.

text: 2.2.4.1 Synchronization and Timing Design 1
trace: 11 2.2.3.3 Baseboard Management Controller --> 2.2.4 Synchronization and Timing --> 2.2.4.1 Synchronization and Timing Design 1

text:
* This section describes the synchronization and timing mechanism that is used in the O-DU7-2.
  * a. Hardware Requirements
  * The O-DU7-2 shall support following timing synchronization methods:
  * 1\. GPS Synchronization
  * 2\. Ethernet based IEEE1588V2 Synchronization
  * 3\. BeiDou Synchronization
  * 4\. BeiDou and GPS switching
trace: 11 2.2.3.3 Baseboard Management Controller --> 2.2.4 Synchronization and Timing --> 2.2.4.1 Synchronization and Timing Design 1

text: b. Hardware Design
trace: 11 2.2.3.3 Baseboard Management Controller --> 2.2.4 Synchronization and Timing --> b. Hardware Design

text: Depending on the timing distribution topologies used, the O-DU7-2 system clock is able to synchronize with the Grand Master Clock \(GMC\) using IEEE1588 via either the front haul NIC or backhaul NIC, or synchronizing timing using Global Navigation Satellite System \(GNSS\). In the case of IEEE1588, the Physical Hardware Clock \(PHC\) within the NIC is synchronized with the GMC first, then the O-DU7-2 system clock is synchronized with the PHC. The O-DU7-2 is also capable to provide clock to the O-RU7-2 via front haul if needed. When GNSS becomes available to O-DU7-2, it will be able to synchronize the system clock to Coordinated Universal Time \(UTC\). Figure 2-7 outlines the O-DU7-2 timing synchronization mechanisms.

text: 2Gb memory capacity is enough. The online debug function is performed by external Ethernet PHY with an RJ45 connector. text: For the O-RU7-2 the sampling function and frequency conversion function can be performed by transceiver. The purpose of using the transceiver is to saving power and size of the PCB. The Transceiver is to convert between high- speed baseband data and a low-level RF for both transmit and receive signal chain. In addition, the transceiver is responsible for orchestration of control signals not limited to the PA enable, LNA enable, LNA bypass as well as other required system level signals.

description:
The diagram depicts the flow of of signals in a digital signal processing system for an ORAN and 5G network:

1. "Clock, Synchronization & Syndrome" from Clock to Receiver/Sender
2. "SERDES OUT" from Receiver/Sender to SPI Port
3. "SERDES IN" from Control Interface to Receiver/Sender
4. "SERDES OUT" from Receiver/Sender to SPI Port
5. "SERDES IN" from Receiver/Sender to DPD Engine and SPI Port
6. "SERDES OUT" from Transmitter/Receiver to SPI Port
7. "DECIMATION" from Receiver to Device Management
8. "INTERPOLATION" from Device Management to Transmitter/Receiver
9. "OVERLOAD" from Device Management to Transmitter/Receiver
10. "SERDES OUT/SERDES IN" between Receiver/Sender and SPI Port
11. "JESD204B/C SERDES IN" from Receiver to Transmitter/Receiver
12. "JESD204B/C SERDES OUT" from Transmitter/Receiver to Receiver
13. "SERDES OUT" from Receiver to Transmitter/Receiver
14. "DECIMATION" from Receiver to Transmitter/Receiver
15. "INTERPOLATION" from Transmitter/Receiver to Device Management
16. "AGC" (Automatic Gain Control) from Device Management to Transmitter/Receiver
17. "RSSI" (Received Signal Strength Indication) feedback from Transmitter/Receiver to Device Management
18. "DEVICE MANAGEMENT" loopback from Device Management to Transmitter/Receiver
19. "OPTIONAL FEATURES" flow from Receiver to Transmitter/Receiver

text:
* REF Clock In is the differential reference input to the on-chip synthesizer. This may also function as the SERDES Device Clock.  
  * SYSREF is a JESD204B/C differential synchronization signal.
  * Ext LO/Clock Input is an optional input that can be used as an alternate LO or clocking signal.
  * Rx1 through Rx4 are differential receiver inputs to their respective cores.
  * Tx1 through Tx4 are differential transmitter output from their respective cores.
  * ORx1 through ORx4 are differential observation receiver inputs.
  * SCLK is the serial control clock input.
  * CSB is the active low device select for the control interface.
  * SDO is the serial data output for the control interface. This pin may be omitted for 3-pin control implementations.
  * SDIO is a bidirectional serial data interface. In 4-pin mode, this pin functions as the serial data input.
  * GPIO1 GPIO\# are general purpose IO signals used for interrupts, enables, test mode and resets. These are used as interface and control for peripheral devices including controllers, TxVGAs, PA, LNA and similar devices where SPI control is too slow.
  * SYNCIN are differential pins associated with the receiver channels of the JESD204 interface. In not used, they are typically grounded. Up to 4 pair may be supported.
  * SERDES Out are differential JESD204B/C data output interfaces. Up to 8 lanes may be active.
  * SERDES In are differential JESD204B/C data input interfaces. Up to 8 lanes may be active.

trace: 11 2.3.2 O-RU7-2 Hardware Components for FPGA based Design --> 16 2.3.2.2.3 Low Noise Amplifier \(LNA\) Reference Design --> • One stage LNA

text: RFin is the input port of the LNA. RFout is the output of the LNA. Vcc is the power input of the LNA. LNA EN is the control pin to disable or enable the LNA. The input match to 50 ohm as much as possible to reduce the reflection. But for output of the LNA, it is hard to get best Noise figure and the output return loss. Compromise is needed between NF and return loss. Usually the return loss should be around -10dB or -12dB. Also should be very careful to assure the stability of the LNA in a large bandwidth. Vcc needs capacitors to reduce the DC power ripples and give a short route to reduce the RF energy leakage. Figure 2-20 shows the details.

trace: 9 2.3.3 O-RU7-2 Hardware Components for SDR based Design --> 2.3.3.2.2 Power Amplifier \(PA\) Reference Design

text: The PA is the final stage that amplifies the downlink RF signal. Considering the requirement of the conducted output power of 24 dBm at the antenna connector and the maximum 3 dB insertion loss between the PA and the antenna, including the directional coupler, the circulator, and the band-pass filter, the PA output power should be at least 27 dBm \(same output power as in 2.3.2.2.2\). The ACLR should be less than -35 dBc \(before applying the DPD\) to ease the hardware processing requirements of the DPD algorithm and still be able to meet the 3GPP TS38.104 ACLR requirements \(clause 6.6.3\). To support TDD mode, the PA should be capable of swiftly turning ON and OFF. The switching time should be less than 1 usec.

text: The RF switch is used to change the RF path from a common port. The insertion loss at the through path should be as small as possible, while the insertion loss at the blocked path should be as large as possible. The first use case is to switch TX and RX path from the antenna port. The second use case is to switch the TX feedback and RX from the RX input of RF transceiver. In the first use case, the common port of the RF switch is connected to port-3 as shown in Figure 2-30. During TX duration, the RF switch is switched to the port of 50 ohms termination.

text: This unit handles multiple high-speed interfaces and digital signal processing. The main chipset is based on FPGA with ARM multi-core processor while FPGA is responsible for high speed data processing and ARM cores are mainly for configuration and management.
trace: 2.4.2 FHM7-2 Hardware Components --> 2.4.2.1 Digital Processing Unit --> b. FPGA Design

text: The FPGA function is shown below:
trace: 2.4.2 FHM7-2 Hardware Components --> 2.4.2.1 Digital Processing Unit --> b. FPGA Design

text: For the uplink processing, the eCPRI interface module is used to receive eCPRI link form O-RU7-2 and generate the reference frequency and time slot for time and frequency synchronization. Then the eCPRI de-frame module gets the uplink IQ bit stream of the time domain the carrier from O-RU7-2. If the uplink IQ stream is compressed, then it needs the de-compression module to translate them into original bit width.
trace: 2.4.2 FHM7-2 Hardware Components --> 2.4.2.1 Digital Processing Unit --> b. FPGA Design

text: After that all the O-RU7-2 uplink IQ streams are combined and the precondition for the combined function is that each stream from different O-RU7-2 is aligned in time domain.
trace: 2.4.2 FHM7-2 Hardware Components --> 2.4.2.1 Digital Processing Unit --> b. FPGA Design

text: Then the time domain IQ date goes to the Low PHY function module to change to frequency domain IQ samples by FFT. Other functions are not specified in detail here.
trace: 2.4.2 FHM7-2 Hardware Components --> 2.4.2.1 Digital Processing Unit --> b. FPGA Design

text: If the FHM7-2 can support two separate cells, then the two cell uplink signal should be aggregated or interleaved together. Then capture the IQ streams in the eCPRI frame and transmitted by eCPRI interface to the O-DU7-2.

text: b. FPGA Design
trace: --> b. FPGA Design

text: This unit handles multiple high-speed interfaces and digital signal processing. The main chipset is based on FPGA with multi-core processor while FPGA is responsible for high speed data processing and processor cores are mainly for configuration and management.

text: For the uplink processing, the CPRI interface module is used to receive CPRI link from O-RU8 for generation of reference frequency and time slot for time and frequency synchronization. Then the CPRI de- frame module gets the uplink IQ bit stream of the time domain the carrier from O-RU8. If the uplink IQ stream is compressed, then it needs the de-compression module to translate them into original bit width. All the O-RU8 uplink IQ streams are combined and the precondition for the combine function is that each stream from different O-RU8 is aligned in time domain. Then the time domain IQ data goes to the Low PHY function module to change to frequency domain IQ samples by performing FFT function.
trace: --> The FPGA function is shown below:

text: If the FHGW7-2-→8 can support two separate cells, then the two cell uplink signal should be aggregated or interleaved together. Then FHGW7-2-→8 should capture the IQ streams in the eCPRI frame and transmit it via eCPRI interface to the O-DU7-2. For the downlink processing, the procedure is very much the same as uplink but in reverse order. The difference is that the downlink signal is duplicated with 8 copies and transmits that to different O-RU8. There is also one eCPRI/CPRI OAM module. Actually this module will work with the processor to accommodate the OAM of different O-RU8 and the FHGW7-2-→8 itself.

For remote power supply, it will support -48V DC via either standalone cable or cat-6A cable. Usually a separated AC-DC power supply is used for the 220V to 48V conversion. text:
* Different eaxc-id correspond to different logical functions, such as cell, carrier, air separation data flow, etc. It
  * identifies the end-to-end data flow from the processing end of the O-DU to the end of the O-RU8 antenna.
  * During the configuration procedure:
  * O-DU should configure the eaxc-id for FHGW7-2→8 U-Plane endpoints.so as to realize the mapping between
  * logical functions and FHGW7-2→8 physical resources. Refer to the YANG model low-level-tx-endpoint and
  * low-level-rx-endpoint in the o-ran-uplane-conf-hub.yang.
  * O-DU should configure the relation between the U-Plane endpoint and the northward e-CPRI data flow for the
  * FHGW7-2→8, to realize the mapping between the northward e-CPRI data flow and the O-RU8 physical resources.
  * O-DU should configure the relation between the U-Plane endpoint and the southward e-CPRI data flow for
  * the FHGW7-2→8, to realize the mapping between the data flow to e-CPRI and the physical resources of O-RU8.
  * See 15.2.4 shared cell for details.
  * O-DU should configure the relation between the U-Plane endpoint and the southward CPRI data flow for the
  * FHGW7-2→8, to realize the mapping between the southward CPRI data flow and the O-RU8 physical resource.
  * See 15.2.4 shared cell for details.
  * In the procedure of data transmission, combined with the 15.2.1.1 CPRI U-Plane data flow model:
  * In the downlink direction, the FHGW7-2→8 obtains the e-CPRI data flow from the e-CPRI interface, finds the
  * corresponding U-Plane Tx endpoint\(low-level-tx-endpoint\) according to eaxc-id, and sends the processed data
  * to the CPRI data flow on the corresponding CPRI interface.
  * In the uplink direction, after the FHGW7-2→8 receives the CPRI data flow from the CPRI interface, it finds the
  * corresponding U-Plane Rx endpoint\(low-level-rx-endpoint\), according to eaxc-id, and sends the processed data
  * to the e-CPRI data flow on the corresponding e-CPRI interface.
  * The rules for configuring eaxc-id by O-DU are as follows:
  * For the same uplink U-Plane data flow,
  * ✓ The low level TX endpoint \(low-level-tx-endpoint\) in FHGW7-2→8 should be configured with the same eaxc-id with TX endpoint \(tx-endpoint\) in O-RU8;
  * For the same downlink U-Plane data flow,
  * ✓ The low level RX endpoint \(low-level-rx-endpoint\) in FHGW7-2→8 should be configurated with the same eaxc-id with the RX endpoint \(rx-endpoint\) in O-RU8;
  * The FHGW7-2→8 should reject configuration requests that violate the above rules.
  * The diagram below shows an example of eaxc-id assignment in the architecture converting from eCPRI Option7 to CPRI Option8.

trace: A4.7 FHGW7-2→8 Delay Management

text: The fronthaul interface between O-DU and FHGW7-2→8 adopts e-CPRI based on Option 7-2x function split defined by ORAN-WG4.CUS.0-v03.00. Its delay management complies with the technical requirements in Section 11.3, "Delay Management of shared Cell".
trace: A4.7 FHGW7-2→8 Delay Management

text: A4.7.1 Convention
trace: A4.7 FHGW7-2→8 Delay Management --> A4.7.1 Convention

text: The current delay measurement and management model is implemented according to the FHGW7-2→8 functional model given in Section 15.2.4. The functional model supports the following combine types:
trace: A4.7 FHGW7-2→8 Delay Management --> A4.7.1 Convention

text: Combine type1: Uplink data from southward CPRI interfaces are combined in CPRI domain, after processed by the Low PHY and output in the format of Option7-2x at the FHGW7-2→8 northward interface, namely uplink data of CPRI domain combined within the FHGW7-2→8.
trace: A4.7 FHGW7-2→8 Delay Management --> A4.7.1 Convention

text: Combine type 2: Southward Option7-2x port \(e-CPRI\) Northward data can be combined in the 7-2x data domain. This mode is the FHM mode of O-RAN Option7-2x shared cell. This method supports the combine of 1~n sub-FHGW7- 2→8 uplinked data at the FHGW7-2→8.
trace: A4.7 FHGW7-2→8 Delay Management --> A4.7.1 Convention

text: Corresponding to Combine type 1, the combine delay of Option8 field is reflected as a part of TBDelayUL. Corresponding to Combine type 2, the combine delay of option7-2x field is reflected as T\_Comb.

text: Section 4.9 DL\_Offset parameter in Option8 O-RU<sub>8</sub> delay management model determines the "data/time" relationship at the FHGW<sub>7-2→8</sub> CPRI outlet. DL\_Offset, CPRI domain T12 of O-RU<sub>8</sub>, T\_Cal\_DL of O-RU<sub>8</sub>, T2a of O-RU<sub>8</sub>, these four parameters determine the occurrence of air port delay of downlink signals in an additive way. Under the current condition of indoor, DL\_Offset is required to have a certain margin because it involves the copy, summations and air port alignment between O-RU<sub>8</sub>, so that the increase or deletion of O-RU<sub>8</sub> in the same copy domain will not cause the delay adjustment of other O-RU<sub>8</sub> in the same cell. Specifically, the delay manager \(O-DU\) is required to reserve sufficient margin when constructing DL\_Offset. The implementation methods are as follows:

text: O-DU can obtain the O-RU8 topological relation \(adjacency relation\) of a shared cell. The shared cell topology discovery procedure is filled in to the ethernet forwarding Information Base \(FIB\) using the LBM/LBR connection check procedure running at the Ethernet layer as defined in Section 3.3.1.5 Connectivity Detection, and FIB is obtained based on O-DU. The difference is that, since the FHGW7-2→8 southward is based on CPRI IQ link, only the Ethernet network-based M-Plane has MAC address, therefore, the LBM/LBR procedure in the 3.3.1.5 Connectivity detection
trace: 9 A4.8.3 Details of Operation --> 11 A4.8.3.1 Topology Discovery

text: section, the FHGW7-2→8 southward is based on M-Plane. Transparent bridge functionality is used for O-RU8 with shared cell functionality running in FHGW7-2→8 and/or cascading mode.
trace: 9 A4.8.3 Details of Operation --> 11 A4.8.3.1 Topology Discovery

text: O-DU determines the topology by the following two-step procedure:
trace: 9 A4.8.3 Details of Operation --> 11 A4.8.3.1 Topology Discovery

text: 1\) In the first phase, the procedure of using the 3.3.1.5 connectivity detection section is used to execute the Ethernet connection monitoring for all the discovered O-RU8 MAC addresses. The echo of the Ethernet loopback from the found MAC address should ensure that the transparent bridge in the FHGW7-2→8 and the cascading mode is automatically learning to pass the MAC addresses of these devices
trace: 9 A4.8.3 Details of Operation --> 11 A4.8.3.1 Topology Discovery

text: Note: In addition to Ethernet connection monitoring, DHCP discovery, Call Home and M-Plane connection establishment can also be used to fill in information in FIB, so maybe O-RU8 has a northward port to do the above.
trace: 9 A4.8.3 Details of Operation --> 11 A4.8.3.1 Topology Discovery

text: 2\) In the second phase, O-DU uses the o-ran-ethernet-forwarding.yang model to discovery which MAC addresses have been learned by the ethernet bridge function. O-DU uses each Ethernet forwarding entry to determine adjacency relationships
trace: 9 A4.8.3 Details of Operation --> 11 A4.8.3.1 Topology Discovery

text:

  * cpri8.yang, and eCPRI7-to-CPRI8 mode was added for the shared-cell-copy-combine mode in o-ran-shared-cell.yang,
  * which is used for the configuration of FHGW7-2→8 connect to O-RU8.
  * COMMON
  * SELECTIVE
  * eCPRI7-to-CPRI8
trace: 9 A4.8.3 Details of Operation --> A4.8.3.3 Configuration of FHGW7-2→8 Connect to O-RU8
9 A4.8.3 Details of Operation --> A4.8.3.3 Configuration of FHGW7-2→8 Connect to O-RU8

text:
* The function of downlink copy of shared-cell-copy-entities-ecpri7-to-cpri8 is configured in two parts.
  * 1\) low-level-tx-endpoint
  * This parameter identifies the data source of the downlink copy of the shared cell, points to the Tx endpoint in the Low
  * PHY U-Plane configuration.
  * 2\) south-node-processing-elements-cpri
  * This parameter identifies the data destination of downlink copy of the shared cell, points to the CPRI flow, which is
  * defined in the CPRI interface YANG model.
trace: 9 A4.8.3 Details of Operation --> A4.8.3.3 Configuration of FHGW7-2→8 Connect to O-RU8
9 A4.8.3 Details of Operation --> A4.8.3.3 Configuration of FHGW7-2→8 Connect to O-RU8

text:
* The function of uplink combination of shared-cell-combine-entities-option8-cpri is configured in two parts
  * 1\) low-level-rx-endpoint
  * This parameter identifies the data destination of the shared cell uplink combine and points to the Rx endpoint in the
  * Low PHY U-Plane configuration.
  * 2\) south-node-processing-elements-cpri
  * This parameter identifies the data source of the downlink copy data of the shared cell and points to the CPRI-Flow
  * defined in the FHGW7-2→8 southward CPRI interface model.
trace: 9 A4.8.3 Details of Operation --> A4.8.3.3 Configuration of FHGW7-2→8 Connect to O-RU8
9 A4.8.3 Details of Operation --> A4.8.3.3 Configuration of FHGW7-2→8 Connect to O-RU8

text:
* Note: In contrast to the shared cell in O-RAN specification, the downlink copy and uplink combine configuration do not
  * define the shared cell U-Plane configuration part. This is because all the U-Plane configuration information \(such as
  * eaxc-id, downlink-radio-frame-offset, downlink-sfn-offset, and N-TA-Offset of uplink only parameter\) is fully defined
  * in the low-level-tx-endpoint of Low PHY U-Plane configuration, and the shared cell part does not need to define it
  * again.
